content.text:
Build an arcade maze-chase game called Lantern Maze (Pac-Man style) on a canvas: a dark navy maze with glowing teal walls, a golden round hero with a chomping mouth, four ghosts whose eyes look where they move (Ember red, Blossom pink, Tide cyan, Marigold orange), and a pixel-style or bold monospace font. Keep drawing light (no per-pixel effects) so it runs smoothly on a laptop without a GPU.

Use exactly this 21 x 21 maze (row 1 on top, column 1 on the left; '#' wall, '.' dot, 'o' power pellet, '-' ghost-house door, 'G' ghost house, 'P' hero start without a dot). Row 10 is a tunnel: leaving one side enters the other.
#####################
#.........#.........#
#o##.####.#.####.##o#
#...................#
#.##.#.#######.#.##.#
#....#....#....#....#
####.####.#.####.####
####.#.........#.####
####.#.###-###.#.####
.......#GGGGG#.......
####.#.#######.#.####
####.#....P....#.####
####.#.#######.#.####
#.........#.........#
#o##.####.#.####.##o#
#..#.............#..#
##.#.#.#######.#.#.##
#....#....#....#....#
#.#######.#.#######.#
#...................#
#####################

Hero: stands on P facing left until the first direction key, then moves 8 tiles/s until a wall stops it. Arrow keys and WASD steer; a direction pressed early is remembered and taken at the next opening.

Ghosts: Ember starts on row 8 just above the door and the other three inside the house; Blossom leaves at once, Tide after 30 dots and Marigold after 60 (or whenever no dot has been eaten for 4 s). At each tile a ghost takes the open, non-reversing direction whose next tile is closest in straight-line distance to its target (ties: up, left, down, right). Chase targets: Ember the hero's tile; Blossom the tile 4 ahead of the hero; Tide the tile 2 ahead of the hero with the vector from Ember to it doubled; Marigold the hero's tile when more than 8 tiles away, otherwise her scatter target. Scatter targets are the corner tiles: Ember row 1 col 21, Blossom row 1 col 1, Tide row 21 col 21, Marigold row 21 col 1. Each life runs scatter 7 s, chase 20 s, scatter 7 s, chase 20 s, scatter 5 s, then chase for good; ghosts reverse at every switch.

Power and points: dots 10, pellets 50. A pellet frightens the ghosts (dark blue, half speed, random turns, flashing white in the last 2 s) for 6 s on level 1, 4 s on level 2 and 2 s on level 3; eating frightened ghosts scores 200, 400, 800, 1600 in a row, and an eaten ghost becomes eyes that fly back to the house. After 70 and 140 dots a fruit appears on P for 9 s (cherry 100, strawberry 300, orange 500 on levels 1-3). Ghosts move at 90, 95 and 100 percent of the hero's speed on levels 1-3 and at half speed in the tunnel.

Flow: 3 lives; touching a normal ghost plays a death animation and resets everyone's position. Clearing all dots and pellets flashes the maze and shows 'LEVEL 2' (then 'LEVEL 3'); clearing level 3 shows 'YOU WIN!'. Losing the last life shows 'GAME OVER'. Each level and each new life begins with 'READY!' for 2 s.

Screens: a title with 'Press Enter to start', a difficulty choice Easy / Normal / Hard (ghost speeds x0.85 / x1 / x1.1) and a TOP 5 table (rank, 3-letter initials, score, level) saved in localStorage; a finished game with a score above 0 that makes the table asks for initials (type letters, then Enter). P or Escape pauses with Resume, Restart and Quit to title. HUD: score, high score, lives and level.

QA debug mode when the URL has ?debug=1: G toggles an overlay that marks each ghost's current target tile with an X in its color, the HUD shows the ghost mode and its time left (e.g. 'SCATTER 4.2s'), N removes every dot and pellet except the 8 dots in the hero's starting corridor on row 12, F starts frightened mode as if a pellet had been eaten, and I toggles invincibility.

## Deliverable
Save the result in `/workspace/output/` as a static web page with entry `index.html`, viewed at a 1280x800 viewport.
It must work offline from that folder alone (relative paths only); there is no internet access.

interaction_hints: Each interact call opens a fresh page; use --entry 'index.html?debug=1' for the debug keys. Rows and columns are 1-based as in the request; the maze has 198 dots and 4 pellets (rows 3 and 15, columns 2 and 20). Start: screenshot the title (TOP 5 table, difficulty), press Enter, wait 2500 (READY!). Buffered turn: press ArrowLeft, wait 100, press ArrowUp: the hero goes left and turns up at column 7 (the first opening), score 40 when it reaches column 7. Tunnel: press ArrowLeft, wait 100, press ArrowUp, wait 400, press ArrowLeft, wait 1200, screenshot: the hero turned left on row 10 and reappeared on the right side (the Left press must land while he climbs from row 12 to row 10; adjust the 400 ms wait between 350 and 500 if needed). Targets (debug): press Enter, wait 2200, press g, screenshot at ~1 s (SCATTER: four X marks in the corners, only Ember and Blossom outside the house), press ArrowLeft, wait until the HUD shows CHASE (7 s), screenshot: Ember's X on the hero's tile, Blossom's X 4 tiles ahead of the hero in his direction, Marigold's X on her corner if she is within 8 tiles; ghosts reverse when the mode switches. (pressing f on level 2 should give ~4 s of fright) and again on level 3 for 'YOU WIN!'. Game over and table: on a plain page press Enter, wait 2500, press ArrowLeft (40 points) and wait up to 60 s with screenshots every 10 s (lives drop, READY! between lives, then 'GAME OVER'); type ABC, press Enter; then do a reload action and screenshot the title (ABC 40). rubric.criterion: The maze matches the given 21x21 map: same walls and corridors, power pellets at rows 3 and 15 in columns 2 and 20, the ghost house with its door on row 9, the open tunnel on row 10 and the hero starting on row 12, column 11; the ghosts are red, pink, cyan and orange.

The hero waits until a key is pressed, then moves continuously and stops at walls; a direction pressed early is taken at the next opening (ArrowLeft then ArrowUp turns up at column 7), and leaving row 10 on one side re-enters on the other.
Dots add 10 and pellets 50 to the HUD score (4 dots to the left of the start give 40), and eaten dots disappear.

With ?debug=1 and G, the target overlay shows the specified rules: in scatter the four X marks sit on their corner tiles; in chase Ember's X is on the hero's tile, Blossom's is 4 tiles ahead of the hero, and Marigold's returns to her corner when she is within 8 tiles.
The debug HUD shows the mode timer switching from SCATTER to CHASE after 7 s with the ghosts reversing, and at the start only Ember and Blossom are outside the house.

A pellet (or F in debug) turns the ghosts dark blue and slower for about 6 s on level 1, flashing white near the end; touching a frightened ghost scores 200 and turns it into eyes that return to the house.
Touching a normal ghost plays a death animation, removes a life and resets positions with 'READY!'; after the third life 'GAME OVER' appears.
Clearing the maze (debug N, then eating the 8 corridor dots) shows 'LEVEL 2' with a refilled maze, level 2 fright lasts about 4 s, and clearing level 3 shows 'YOU WIN!'.
After a game with points, 3-letter initials can be entered; the TOP 5 table on the title shows rank, initials, score and level in descending order and survives a page reload.
P or Escape freezes the game with Resume, Restart and Quit to title options that work, and the title offers Easy, Normal and Hard.
The maze and HUD are centered and fully visible in 1280x800 with square tiles, and HUD text never overlaps the maze.
A polished arcade look a game artist would accept: consistent glowing teal wall outlines, a hero with an animated mouth, ghosts with eyes that follow their direction, and crisp readable HUD type.

content.text:
Build the FY2026 Q4 board review deck for Lumenstack, a B2B observability software company, presented by CEO Daniel Reyes and CFO Priya Natarajan to the board on 22 July 2026. Every number must come from your own analysis of the two files provided: arr_movements.csv (monthly new, expansion, contraction and churned ARR in $K per segment, July 2024 to June 2026) and account_executives.csv (FY2026 quota and closed ARR in $K per account executive).

Definitions: the fiscal year runs July to June (FY2026 = July 2025 to June 2026). ARR on 1 July 2024 was Enterprise 6,240, Mid-Market 4,180 and SMB 2,310 ($K). Month-end ARR = previous ARR + new + expansion - contraction - churned. NRR = (ARR at 30 June 2025 + FY2026 expansion - contraction - churned) / ARR at 30 June 2025; GRR is the same without expansion. Attainment = closed / quota. Show ARR in $M with two decimals (one decimal for chart totals), percentages with one decimal and bridge steps in whole $K.

Exactly 14 slides, with these titles:
1. 'FY2026 Q4 Board Review' (company name, date and both presenters)
2. 'Agenda': Performance, Retention, Sales efficiency, FY2027 plan
3. 'FY2026 at a glance': KPI tiles for ending ARR, year-over-year ARR growth, NRR and GRR
4. 'ARR by segment': stacked bar chart of quarter-end ARR, Q1 FY25 to Q4 FY26, stacked by segment, total above each bar
5. 'Net new ARR by month': line chart of the 24 monthly values with a dashed 3-month moving average; annotate the highest and lowest months with their values
6. 'FY2026 ARR bridge': waterfall from ARR at 30 June 2025 through new, expansion, contraction and churn to ARR at 30 June 2026 (increases green, decreases red, totals in the accent color, thin connectors)
7. 'Retention by segment': table with rows Enterprise, Mid-Market, SMB, Total and columns Ending ARR, YoY growth, NRR, GRR, Share of ARR; the lowest NRR cell highlighted red
8. 'Tenure drives attainment': scatter of tenure (x) vs attainment (y) for every account executive, a dashed 100% line, a least-squares trend line labeled with its slope (points per month, two decimals) and R² (two decimals), plus the team attainment (total closed / total quota)
9. 'Land-and-expand motion': left-to-right process diagram Free trial → Team plan → Platform deal → Enterprise agreement, arrows labeled 22%, 35% and 41%
10. 'FY2027 targets': an ARR target equal to FY2026 ending ARR grown 35%, NRR 102%, GRR 88%
11. 'Risks and mitigations': three risks, each with a mitigation and an owner
12. 'Decisions for the board': three numbered decisions
13. 'Appendix: metric definitions'
14. 'Appendix: account executive detail': all 16 account executives in one table sorted by attainment, highest first

Master layout: white slides, Inter only, one indigo accent (#4F46E5). On slides 2-14 the title is an h2 in Inter 700 at 34px whose left edge is 64px from the slide edge, at the same top position on every slide; a section tracker at the top right lists the four agenda sections in 12px capitals with the current one in the accent color (Performance = slides 3-5, Retention = 6-7, Sales efficiency = 8-9, FY2027 plan = 10-12; slides 2, 13 and 14 highlight none); a footer with a hairline rule shows 'Lumenstack · Board confidential' on the left and the slide number as 'n / 14' on the right. Draw every chart as inline SVG with titled axes; no text smaller than 12px.

Presenter mode: only slide 1 is visible on load. ArrowRight, Space and PageDown go forward; ArrowLeft and PageUp go back; Home and End jump to the first and last slide; the URL hash follows the slide (#5 for slide 5) and opening slides.html#5 starts on slide 5. Every slide carries 1-3 sentences of speaker notes in an aside with class notes that stays hidden on the slide; pressing N toggles a panel showing the current slide's notes. The slide 6 notes must state FY2026 net new ARR in $K; the slide 8 notes must name the account executives at or above 100% of quota.

## Deliverable
Save the result in `/workspace/output/` as a single HTML slide deck `slides.html` in which every slide is an element with class `slide`, exactly 1280x720 px, in document order, with its content fitting inside the slide.
It must work offline from that folder alone (relative paths only); there is no internet access.
Task files are in `/workspace/task/`: `arr_movements.csv`, `account_executives.csv`.

content.text:
Recreate the attached national park badge as a hand-written SVG with viewBox 0 0 600 600. It is a circular emblem on a cream square: a deep green disc with a ring of cream dots and a thin cream line inside it, the words EVERGREEN RIDGE set along the top arc and NATIONAL PARK along the bottom arc (both upright and reading left to right), and a small star at 9 and at 3 o'clock.

The inner scene is clipped to a circle with a thick cream frame and a thin frame line just outside it: a coral-to-gold sky with a sunburst of alternating light rays behind a pale sun with a halo, two birds, a purple back range with two snowcaps, a green middle range, diagonal hatching on the shaded slopes, a dark lake with a winding golden river and white ripple strokes, and layered dark pine trees on both sides. A rust ribbon banner with darker folded tails and dashed stitching along both edges crosses the lower part and reads EST. 1921 along its curve.

Use textPath for all curved text, a clipPath for the scene and a pattern for the hatching. Match positions, proportions, colors and letter spacing as closely as you can.

## Deliverable
Save the result in `/workspace/output/` as a standalone SVG file `badge.svg` (pure vector: no embedded raster images, no scripts).
Task files are in `/workspace/task/`: `reference.png`.
The target is `/workspace/task/reference.png` (also attached).
Rebuild it with real markup/vector/code; do not embed, trace or copy the target image.

title: Recreate a vintage national park badge with curved text
prompt:
Recreate the attached national park badge as a hand-written SVG with viewBox 0 0 600 600. It is a circular emblem on a cream square: a deep green disc with a ring of cream dots and a thin cream line inside it, the words EVERGREEN RIDGE set along the top arc and NATIONAL PARK along the bottom arc (both upright and reading left to right), and a small star at 9 and at 3 o'clock.

The inner scene is clipped to a circle with a thick cream frame and a thin frame line just outside it: a coral-to-gold sky with a sunburst of alternating light rays behind a pale sun with a halo, two birds, a purple back range with two snowcaps, a green middle range, diagonal hatching on the shaded slopes, a dark lake with a winding golden river and white ripple strokes, and layered dark pine trees on both sides. A rust ribbon banner with darker folded tails and dashed stitching along both edges crosses the lower part and reads EST. 1921 along its curve.

Use textPath for all curved text, a clipPath for the scene and a pattern for the hatching. Match positions, proportions, colors and letter spacing as closely as you can.

rubric.criterion: Overall structure matches: green disc nearly filling the cream square, dotted ring and thin ring near the rim, text band, circular scene about two thirds of the badge diameter with a thick cream frame plus a thin outer frame line, and the ribbon across the lower part of the scene.

Curved text: 'EVERGREEN RIDGE' along the top arc and 'NATIONAL PARK' along the bottom arc, both upright, left to right, centred, in heavy cream capitals with wide letter spacing (top text slightly larger); five-point cream stars at 9 and 3 o'clock.

Sky: vertical gradient from coral at the top through orange to pale gold at the horizon, about 24 alternating light rays radiating from the sun, and a pale sun disc with a soft halo just above the mountains in the centre; two small dark birds upper left.

Mountains: a purple back range whose highest snowcapped peak is left of centre with a second smaller snowcap further left, a green middle range in front, and diagonal hatch shading on the right-hand slopes of the peaks.

Foreground: dark green lake band, a winding golden-to-blue river from the lake down to the bottom with short white ripple strokes, and dark three-tier pine trees clustered at the left and right edges.
Ribbon: a rust curved banner with darker folded tails extending past the scene frame on both sides, dashed cream stitching along both edges, and 'EST. 1921' following the ribbon's curve.
Colors match the target palette: deep green, cream, rust, coral/orange/gold sky, muted purple and sage green mountains, near-black pines.

Technique as requested: curved text uses textPath (not per-letter rotated text), the scene is clipped with a clipPath, the hatching uses a pattern; The file is built from real vector elements (paths, shapes, gradients, patterns, text), with no embedded image and no traced mesh of hundreds of tiny shapes.

content.text:
Produce a 24-second animated data explainer for the Meridia Energy Agency about rooftop solar. The data is in solar.csv (columns year, province, capacity_mw, share_pct: installed rooftop capacity in megawatts and the share of homes with rooftop solar, in percent) for the eight provinces of Meridia from 2015 to 2024. Every number on screen must come from the CSV.

Format: 1280x720, 30 fps, exactly 24 s (720 frames). Four scenes of 6 s each. The scene boundaries are at 6, 12 and 18 s, and each boundary is a 0.5 s transition centred on it (5.75 to 6.25 s, 11.75 to 12.25 s, 17.75 to 18.25 s):
- at 6 s a cross-dissolve;
- at 12 s a push: scene 2 slides out to the left while scene 3 slides in from the right, ease-in-out;
- at 18 s an iris: scene 4 is revealed inside a circle that grows from the centre of the frame until it covers everything.

Scene 1, 'Capacity is soaring': a line chart of national capacity (the sum over the provinces) per year, with a y axis from 0 to 3,000 MW (gridlines every 500) and a year axis. rubric.criterion: Scene 1 values: a frame at about 5.5 s shows the national line with ten points from 2015 to 2024 that match the CSV totals (spot-check at least three against the y axis or labels: 855 MW in 2015, 1,845 MW in 2020, 2,772 MW in 2024), and the tip label reads 2,772 MW.

The line draws on the stated schedule: a frame at about 2.6 s shows the line through 2019 (tip label 1,643 MW) but not yet reaching 2020, and the callout 'Doubled by 2020' is attached to the 2020 point from about 3.0 s on (absent at 2.6 s; any other year is wrong).

Scene 2 final state (frame at about 11.5 s, year 2024): all eight bars in this order with these values: Brisa Coast 650, Aldena 505, Galen Plains 412, Corvel 385, Dunmore 270, Estrel Valley 225, Highmark 180, Farrow Hills 145.

Rank swaps happen at the right years, with the year counter agreeing: at about 7.5 s (2017) Corvel is still above Brisa Coast and Estrel Valley above Galen Plains; at about 8.0 s (2018) Brisa Coast is above Corvel and Galen Plains above Estrel Valley; at about 9.0 s (2020) Aldena still leads; at about 9.5 s (2021) Brisa Coast has taken first place.

Scene 3 tile colors follow the bins: at about 17.0 s (2024) Brisa Coast is #B45309; Corvel and Galen Plains #F59E0B; Aldena, Dunmore and Highmark #FBBF24; Estrel Valley and Farrow Hills #FDE68A. At about 14.5 s (2020) Brisa Coast is #FBBF24, Farrow Hills and Highmark #FEF3C7 and the other five #FDE68A. Tiles show name and share (e.g. Corvel 30.2% in 2024).

The tile map uses the specified arrangement (Highmark and Farrow Hills on top; Galen Plains, Aldena, Corvel, Dunmore in the middle row; Brisa Coast and Estrel Valley at the bottom) with a five-bin legend; colors cross-fade (a frame at about 13.5 s shows in-between colors) and the year label reads 2015 at 12.8 s, 2020 at 14.5 s and 2024 at 17.0 s.

Scene 4 KPI values are exactly (frame at about 23 s): 2,772 MW total capacity; +224% growth; fastest-growing Highmark ×6.0 (not Brisa Coast, the largest absolute gain); 3 of 8 provinces at 30% or more.

KPI cards enter one at a time: a frame at about 19.0 s shows the first card with its number still counting and at most two cards present (the third and fourth absent); all four numbers are final by about 20.8 s.

content.text:
Build a small multi-page website for Ember & Oak, a small-batch coffee roaster that sells a bean subscription. It should feel warm, premium and hand-crafted. Deliver one index.html that uses hash routing with four routes: #/ (Home), #/beans, #/subscribe and #/faq.

Routing: the header nav (Home, Beans, Subscribe, FAQ) marks the current route with aria-current='page' and a visible active style. document.title is 'Ember & Oak · Small-batch coffee' on Home and '<Page> · Ember & Oak' elsewhere (for example 'Beans · Ember & Oak'). Only the current view is shown, the browser Back button returns to the previous route, opening index.html without a hash shows Home, and any unknown hash such as #/shop shows a 'Page not found' view with a 'Back to home' link.

Home: the headline 'Coffee worth waking up for', a 'Build your subscription' button that goes to #/subscribe, and three steps illustrated with inline SVG.

Beans: six coffee cards with name, origin, roast, tasting notes and price per 250g bag: Kiambu AA (Kenya, Light, $19), Huila Pink Bourbon (Colombia, Light, $21), Yirgacheffe Kochere (Ethiopia, Light, $18), Cerrado Natural (Brazil, Medium, $15), Antigua Pastoral (Guatemala, Medium, $16) and Sumatra Mandheling (Indonesia, Dark, $17). Add roast filter buttons All, Light, Medium and Dark, a sort select (Price: low to high, Price: high to low, Name A–Z) that combines with the filter, and a line such as 'Showing 3 of 6 coffees'.

Subscribe: a plan builder with bag size (250g or 1kg), bags per delivery (a stepper from 1 to 4 that cannot go outside that range) and frequency (Every week, Every 2 weeks, Every month); the default is 250g, 1 bag, Every month. Subscription bags are the roaster's choice at a flat price: $16 per 250g bag and $54 per 1kg bag. Weekly gets 10% off, every 2 weeks 5% off, monthly no discount. Shipping is $5.00 per delivery, or Free when the discounted per-delivery subtotal is $40.00 or more. A live summary shows Subtotal (before discount), Discount, Shipping, Per delivery (discounted subtotal plus shipping) and Per month (per delivery × 4, 2 or 1 deliveries), always in dollars with two decimals; the default shows $21.00 per delivery and $21.00 per month. Save the builder choices in localStorage and restore them after a reload.

FAQ: five questions in an accessible accordion: each question is a button with aria-expanded, and clicking one toggles only its own answer.

At 390px wide the nav collapses into a menu button that opens the four links, and the bean cards and the builder fit the screen.

## Deliverable
Save the result in `/workspace/output/` as a static web page with entry `index.html`, viewed at a 1280x800 viewport.
It must work offline from that folder alone (relative paths only); there is no internet access.

interaction_hints: Routes: in one interact call use eval to set location.hash to '#/beans', '#/subscribe', '#/faq' and '#/shop' (wait 300 ms after each) and eval document.title plus document.querySelector('[aria-current=page]')?.textContent each time; then eval history.back() and check the previous view returns; also click the nav links themselves. Deep link: eval location.hash='#/faq', then reload and screenshot. Beans: click text=Light, then use select on the sort control (find its selector in the source) with 'Price: high to low', screenshot; then All with 'Price: low to high' and 'Name A–Z'. Subscribe: click the size, stepper and frequency controls to reach each rubric scenario and screenshot the summary; press minus at 1 bag and plus at 4 bags to check clamping. Persistence: in one call choose 1kg, 3 bags, Every 2 weeks, reload (re-open #/subscribe if needed), screenshot. FAQ: click two questions and eval their aria-expanded values. Mobile: run interact with --width 390 --height 844 and take full_page screenshots. Click the menu button there.

rubric.criterion: The nav has Home, Beans, Subscribe and FAQ; the current route's link has aria-current='page' and a visible active style, and document.title is exactly 'Ember & Oak · Small-batch coffee' on Home, 'Beans · Ember & Oak', 'Subscribe · Ember & Oak' and 'FAQ · Ember & Oak' on the other routes.

Routing works: nav clicks switch views and the hash without a full reload, only one view is visible at a time, history.back() returns to the previous view, and loading index.html#/faq directly shows the FAQ.
An unknown hash such as #/shop shows a 'Page not found' view whose 'Back to home' link returns to Home; index.html without a hash shows Home.
Home shows the headline 'Coffee worth waking up for', three SVG-illustrated steps, and a 'Build your subscription' button that navigates to #/subscribe.

Beans filter and sort combine: Light shows exactly Kiambu AA, Huila Pink Bourbon and Yirgacheffe Kochere with 'Showing 3 of 6 coffees', and with 'Price: high to low' they are ordered $21, $19, $18; All with 'Price: low to high' runs from Cerrado Natural $15 to Huila Pink Bourbon $21; 'Name A–Z' starts with Antigua Pastoral and ends with Yirgacheffe Kochere.

The builder math is exact: the default shows Per delivery $21.00 and Per month $21.00; 250g, 2 bags, Every 2 weeks shows Subtotal $32.00, Discount $1.60, Shipping $5.00, Per delivery $35.40, Per month $70.80; 1kg, 1 bag, Every week shows Discount $5.40, Shipping Free, Per delivery $48.60, Per month $194.40.
250g, 2 bags, Every week shows Per delivery $33.80 and Per month $135.20, and the bag stepper cannot go below 1 or above 4.
After choosing 1kg, 3 bags and Every 2 weeks and reloading, the builder restores those choices and shows Per delivery $153.90 and Per month $307.80.
The FAQ has five questions rendered as buttons whose aria-expanded flips between true and false; clicking one opens or closes only its own answer.
At 390px the nav is a menu button that reveals the four links, the bean cards stack in one column, and the builder controls and summary fit without clipping or overlap.
It looks like a premium roaster: a warm, consistent palette, a clear type hierarchy, even spacing between sections, and summary amounts aligned in a column.
